parole.testo: From Jamaican Creole ganja (“marijuana”), borrowed from Hindi गांजा (gāñjā), ultimately from Sanskrit गञ्जा (gañjā, “hemp”).

parole.significato: plantain tart, a type of patty filled with plantain, treated locally as a variety of empanada.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Jamaican Creole plantain taat (“plantain tart”).

parole.significato: run down (a Caribbean soup consisting of seafood and coconut milk, among other ingredients)
To con or steal from someone, especially in a bold, flagrant manner.
parole.testo: From Jamaican Creole ginnal (“a deceiver; a con artist”).
